markdown_report:
Starting-point insights: (1) SASRec’s causal representation can combine recent and older interests, motivating explicit control over their contributions. User feedback identifies both current intent and sustained narrow preferences as useful signals. (2) Electronics has 14.95% negative-over-positive rankings and a −0.4812 lower-decile margin, motivating stronger ranking supervision. These training diagnostics do not establish validation performance. (3) Similar embedding-similarity scores across categories weaken the case for prioritizing collapse regularization. None establishes equipment ownership or compatibility.

Related-work insights: (1) TLSRec provides precedent for separating long- and short-term preferences, supporting a lightweight fusion experiment. Its results do not establish gains here. (2) gSASRec motivates training with more negatives and calibrated objectives, directly relevant to weak separation. Objective choice still requires validation. (3) UFNRec highlights false-negative uncertainty, supporting conservative sampling rather than aggressive hard-negative suppression.

The framework organizes research into representation timescale, ranking supervision, and behavioral evidence:

| Direction | Existing approach | Proposed experiment | Remaining gap |
|---|---|---|---|
| Timescale | SASRec; TLSRec | Recent-window residual gate | Sparse prefixes |
| Supervision | gSASRec | Uniform multi-negative softmax | Unobserved relevant negatives |
| Association | Directed transition models | Sparse ordered-transition residual | Compatibility remains unknown |

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores are 0–10; higher difficulty means harder. Each cell gives a score and positive/negative assessment.

| Idea | Originality | Potential | User alignment | Model alignment | Difficulty |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| A: gated recent residual with multi-negative ranking | 4: useful combination / established components | 7: portable / uncertain sparse-data benefit | 8: recent plus sustained intent / no compatibility evidence | 8: stronger separation objective / margins may mislead | 4: small branch / predictor changes |
| B: calibrated multi-negative gBCE | 3: established method / little novelty | 7: scalable / tuning dependent | 5: sharper ranking / no explicit intent mechanism | 8: targets separation / false negatives remain | 3: local loss change / calibration required |
| C: directed transition residual | 5: explicit order / familiar association model | 6: interpretable / sparse transitions | 6: plausible next actions / no proof of utility | 6: extra ranking evidence / head-item bias | 5: sparse counts / serving integration |

Select **A** at 0% progress: it balances feasibility with a testable mechanism. The recent branch targets broad associations displacing current mood or task; the retained SASRec branch preserves repeated narrow preferences against incidental recent behavior. Multi-negative supervision targets Electronics’ weak-separation tail. These are hypotheses, not demonstrated improvements.

```python
h = sasrec(prefix)
r = mean(item_embedding(prefix[-window:]))
g = sigmoid(linear(concat(h, r, log1p(prefix_length))))
z = layer_norm(h + g * project(r))
loss = cross_entropy(scores(z, [target] + uniform_negatives), target_index=0)
```

Construct every feature from each causal prefix. Exclude padding, target collisions, and prefix-observed items from negatives; unresolved false negatives remain. Compare baseline, loss-only, residual-only, and combined variants under the shared budget. Select solely by pinned four-category macro validation HR@10; retain seeds, splits, routing, and single-GPU execution. Update the predictor writer and diagnostic adapter to score the same fused features. Report sampled margins as diagnostics, never as benchmark gains.

idea.description: Add a learned recent-window residual to SASRec and train the fused representation with uniform multi-negative softmax. Preserve SASRec’s longer-history representation while learning how much recent context contributes.
idea.motivation: Explicitly targets two observed user failures: broad associations outranking current intent, and incidental associations displacing sustained narrow preferences. Multi-negative training addresses the observed weak positive–negative separation, especially in Electronics. It cannot establish compatibility, ownership, or whether a purchase satisfied a need.
idea.implementation_notes: Use per-position causal window pooling during training and the identical final-prefix computation during inference. Start with window=5 and 16 uniform negatives as experimental defaults, not validated optima. Mask padding, target collisions, and prefix-observed negatives. Preserve DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, all four dataset routes, and SASREC_EPOCHS default 200. Store checkpoints and architecture configuration beneath the trial directory. Update the predictor writer to reconstruct the fusion branch. Retain DiagnosisProbe(view, device).run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), returning metrics and metric_definitions; expose the actual trained module through view.model and fused representations through log2feats. Compute margins through predict_score. Mark unavailable category breakdowns unavailable rather than fabricating metadata. Evaluate the simulator’s twenty training users with unseen full-catalog recommendations; use only pinned macro validation HR@10 for selection. No implementation or performance result is claimed here.
idea.pseudocode:
For each category independently:
  Initialize SASRec and recent-window projection/gate with seed 42.
  For each causal training prefix and target:
    h = SASRec(prefix)
    r = mean(nonpadding item embeddings in last w prefix positions)
    g = sigmoid(Wg [h; r; log(1 + prefix_length)] + bg)
    z = LayerNorm(h + g * Wr(r))
    negatives = sample K uniform eligible item IDs
    logits = dot(z, embedding([target] + negatives))
    optimize cross_entropy(logits, target_index=0)
  Save model state and fusion configuration under the trial directory.
  Emit working/predict.py implementing the same feature and score functions.
Compare controlled ablations using unchanged host validation; retain the best macro HR@10 configuration.

originality.positive: Combines explicit recent-context control with stronger ranking supervision in a small, testable extension.
originality.negative: Both temporal fusion and multi-negative objectives have substantial prior art.

future_potential.positive: A lightweight mechanism supports interpretable ablations across datasets with different intent persistence.
future_potential.negative: Sparse histories may make the gate unreliable, and stronger training margins may not improve held-out HR@10.

code_difficulty.positive: Requires a pooled branch, a gate, and a local objective change using existing embeddings.
code_difficulty.negative: Causal per-position pooling, negative masking, checkpoint loading, and diagnostic compatibility require careful integration.

related_work.title: Self-Attentive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Introduces causal self-attention for sequential recommendation and supplies the starting architecture.
limitations: Does not explicitly establish current practical needs, compatibility, or purchase satisfaction from interaction histories.

related_work.title: TLSRec: Time-Lag Sensitive Sequential Recommendation
contributions: Provides precedent for combining hierarchical long- and short-term preferences with time-sensitive fusion.
limitations: Does not establish improvement under the pinned four-category RecHarness evaluation.

related_work.title: gSASRec
contributions: Motivates additional negatives and calibrated generalized binary cross-entropy to address sampling-related overconfidence.
limitations: Does not establish that the proposed softmax objective or fusion branch improves this benchmark.

related_work.title: UFNRec
contributions: Addresses false-negative uncertainty using teacher-generated soft labels and consistency regularization.
limitations: Uniform sampling and observed-positive masking do not resolve the uncertainty addressed by this method.
